title: SSH Terminal
entryHint: The router's command line over SSH
nothingSelected: Select text in the terminal first (long press)

hostKey.title: Confirm the router's SSH fingerprint
hostKey.message: This is the first SSH connection to this router. Check the fingerprint: once confirmed, the app trusts only this key and stops the connection if it ever changes.
hostKey.changedTitle: The router's SSH fingerprint has changed
hostKey.changedMessage: The router shows a different fingerprint than the one pinned before. A reset or a firmware flash can create new keys; so can someone pretending to be this router. Continue only if you know it is the first.

password.title: SSH Password
password.hint: The password of the router's root account, for this connection only
password.refused: The router refused this password. Try again

error.keyRefused: The router does not accept the app's key. Install the public key again in the router's settings, or log in with the password.
error.unreachable: Can't reach the router's SSH (port {{port}}). Check that SSH (dropbear) is running on the router and that no firewall rule blocks the port.

settings.footer: SSH logs in as root with the router's admin password. A key made by the app works too, without typing a password.
settings.forgotHostKey: Forgotten: it will be confirmed again next time
settings.install: Install the Key on the Router
settings.installed: The key is on the router
settings.remove: Remove the Key from the Router
settings.removed: Removed the key from the router
settings.notActive: Switch to this router to install or remove the key
settings.installTitle: Add the app's public key to the router?
settings.installConsequenceFile: Adds one line to /etc/dropbear/authorized_keys; other keys stay
settings.installConsequenceLogin: This phone can then log in over SSH without a password; remove it here at any time
settings.removeTitle: Remove the app's public key from the router?
settings.removeConsequence: Only the app's own line goes; log in with the password afterwards
